title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification. METHODS: We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses. RESULTS: A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55–39.30]; P =0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68–9.24]; P <0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19–5.34]; P =0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events ( P =0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15–0.82]). CONCLUSIONS: In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT02898610.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In noncardioembolic stroke patients, a CTA-based carotid Plaque-RADS score ≥3 strongly predicted recurrent ipsilateral stroke (aHR 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55–39.30], P=0.01) and MACE (aHR 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19–5.34], P=0.02). Plaque-RADS ≥3 also identified patients with greater MACE reduction from colchicine (HR 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15–0.82], interaction P=0.047).

title: Contemporary US Practice Patterns Regarding Anticoagulation and LAA Closure in ICH Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal secondary stroke prevention remains uncertain for patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Anticoagulation reduces ischemic stroke in AF but increases hemorrhage. Left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion is emerging as an alternative to anticoagulation, but few data exist on its safety in patients with ICH. Amid this uncertainty, little is known about US practice patterns in this scenario. METHODS: We performed a study using linked electronic health record, pharmacy, and insurance claims data on >11 million patients at 29 US healthcare organizations, each with multiple hospital sites, in the TriNetX Linked platform. Validated International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes were used to identify adults with AF hospitalized for ICH during 2016 to 2024. To identify antiplatelet and anticoagulant prescriptions, we used RxNorm codes, a standardized drug naming system from the National Library of Medicine. LAA occlusion was defined using validated Current Procedural Terminology codes. Kaplan-Meier statistics were used to calculate cumulative rates of therapy utilization from discharge through 5 years. We created 3 mutually exclusive treatment groups with censoring at LAA occlusion for analyses of antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy and at anticoagulation for analyses of antiplatelet therapy. RESULTS: We identified 2276 patients with AF hospitalized with ICH. Their mean age was 65.4 (±12.8) years, 40.6% were female, median CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score was 5 (interquartile range, 5–6), 19.6% had Medicare, 26.9% received an anticoagulant prescription within 90 days before ICH, and half were discharged home or to an acute rehabilitation facility. Cumulative 5-year rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%–64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%–46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%–7.6%) for LAA occlusion. LAA occlusion rates did not differ by index ICH date ( P =0.88). CONCLUSIONS: In a contemporary, multicenter US cohort of patients with ICH and AF, 60% were prescribed anticoagulation after discharge, and the remainder were mostly treated with antiplatelet therapy only. These findings suggest widespread use of different secondary stroke prevention strategies in patients with AF and ICH.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In this multicenter US cohort of 2276 atrial fibrillation survivors of intracerebral hemorrhage, cumulative 5-year secondary stroke prevention rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%–64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%–46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%–7.6%) for left atrial appendage occlusion, demonstrating widespread practice variation.

title: Association of Hemispheric Laterality With Neurosurgical Intervention in Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Posthoc Bayesian Analysis of ATACH-2 and ERICH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemispheric laterality influences clinical management in stroke. Given the increasing enthusiasm for surgical management of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), we evaluated the association of hemispheric laterality with the likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention and subsequent 90-day functional outcomes. METHODS: This post hoc analysis included 3477 patients with supratentorial ICH from 2 prospective studies: the ATACH-2 trial (Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage II), conducted at 110 sites in the United States, Japan, China, Taiwan, South Korea, and Germany (2011–2015), and the ERICH study (Ethnic/Racial Variations of Intracerebral Hemorrhage), conducted across 19 centers in the United States (2010–2015). The primary outcome was neurosurgical intervention (hematoma evacuation, decompressive craniectomy, or other craniotomy). Secondary outcomes included external ventricular drain placement, 90-day modified Rankin Scale score, and EuroQOL domains. Hierarchical Bayesian regression models estimating the association between ICH laterality and outcomes were adjusted for age, admission Glasgow Coma Scale, ICH location, ICH volume, and intraventricular hemorrhage. RESULTS: Of 3477 patients, right hemispheric ICH was associated with a higher likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention (adjusted odds ratio, 1.65 [95% credible interval, 1.28–2.14]) and external ventricular drain placement (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% credible interval, 1.04–1.44]) compared with left hemispheric ICH. This association was directionally consistent across ICH locations, study cohorts, and prior specifications. Despite the lower rates of surgical intervention in left hemispheric ICH, there was no meaningful difference in 90-day functional outcomes in patients with left and right hemispheric ICH. CONCLUSIONS: Right hemispheric ICH is associated with a higher likelihood of neurosurgical intervention compared with left hemispheric ICH, though 90-day functional outcomes remain similar between groups. Although these findings highlight a potential laterality-associated variation in neurosurgical intervention, residual confounding from unmeasured anatomic severity and family preferences cannot be excluded. Prospective studies are needed to delineate the explicit clinical and prognostic drivers of surgical decision-making to optimize treatment allocation in ICH. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT01176565 and NCT01202864.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Right hemispheric intracerebral hemorrhage is associated with a significantly higher likelihood of neurosurgical intervention (aOR, 1.65; 95% CrI, 1.28–2.14) and external ventricular drain placement (aOR, 1.22; 95% CrI, 1.04–1.44) compared to left hemispheric hemorrhage, despite similar 90-day functional outcomes between groups.

title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti–factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models. RESULTS: Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35–3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55–1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24–2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44–1.25]; P =0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25–4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38–3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0–2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84–1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28–4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) demonstrate comparable efficacy and safety to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for cerebral venous thrombosis, with similar rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55–1.53]), major bleeding (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44–1.25], *P*=0.26), and good functional outcomes (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.11]), supporting DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO—with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals—would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns. METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021–2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25–4.18]; P =0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P =0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P =0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13–9.62]; P =0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis’ benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P =0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant ( P =0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In this post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial, nonatherosclerotic basilar artery occlusion showed significant benefit within <6 hours (RR, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25–4.18]; P=0.007), whereas atherosclerotic occlusions demonstrated functional improvement (common OR, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13–9.62]; P=0.029) in the ≥6-hour window, suggesting greater time tolerance in atherosclerotic disease.

title: A Recurrent 3′ UTR Variant in CAPN3 Highlights the Diagnostic Impact of Non‐Coding Variants in Limb‐Girdle Muscular Dystrophies
abstract: Objective: A substantial proportion of individuals with suspected genetic conditions, including neuromuscular disorders, lack a definitive molecular diagnosis. Non‐coding variants, particularly those in the 3′ untranslated region (3´UTR), which regulate mRNA stability, translation, and localization, may underlie part of this gap. We investigated the clinical, genetic, and functional relevance of a novel 3′UTR variant in CAPN3 in individuals with persistent hyperCKemia, most of whom also presented with proximal muscle weakness. Methods: Clinical assessment, including muscle biopsy and muscle magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), was performed in individuals harboring the CAPN3 c.*534T>C variant. In silico analyses included the assessment of miRNA binding, mRNA secondary structure, creation or disruption of a poly‐A tail, and RNA‐binding protein (RBP) motifs. A luciferase reporter assay with the c.*534T>C and reference sequence, in the presence or absence of RBFOX1 co‐expression, was performed. Results: We identified 13 individuals from 11 unrelated families presenting with persistent hyperCKemia, commonly accompanied by proximal muscle weakness and myalgia, all harboring the c.*534T>C variant in combination with a previously identified heterozygous CAPN3 variant. Western blot analyses consistently demonstrated absent or markedly reduced calpain‐3 expression, and muscle RNA sequencing (RNAseq) showed reduced CAPN3 levels. In silico analyses indicated that the c.*534T>C variant creates a novel binding site for the RNA‐binding protein RBFOX1. Luciferase reporter assays supported a regulatory effect of the identified variant on calpain‐3 expression. Interpretation: Our results show that a recurrent non‐coding CAPN3 variant causes disease by disrupting post‐transcriptional regulation and demonstrate a generalizable principle, as 3′UTR variants can affect mRNA stability and protein expression across neuromuscular and other Mendelian diseases. Although often difficult to interpret as pathogenic, these variants can be therapeutically actionable, highlighting the importance of systematically investigating non‐coding regions in unsolved genetic cases. ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: A recurrent non-coding 3′UTR variant in *CAPN3* (c.*534T>C) causes autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and persistent hyperCKemia by disrupting post-transcriptional regulation and reducing protein expression. Systematically evaluating non-coding regions in genetically unsolved neuromuscular cases is crucial for diagnostic resolution and therapeutic actionability.

title: Accelerated Epigenetic Aging in Frontotemporal Dementia Highlights Smoking, Inflammation, and Metabolic Signals
abstract: Objective: Epigenetic clocks are biomarkers of biological aging influenced by lifestyle and systemic factors. Accelerated epigenetic aging has been associated with neurodegeneration, but its relevance in frontotemporal dementia is unclear. We investigated biological aging in frontotemporal dementia using the GrimAge2 epigenetic clock, a DNA methylation‐based predictor of mortality, and examined the contribution of smoking‐related DNA methylation. Methods: Peripheral blood DNA methylation data from frontotemporal dementia patients and controls from 2 independent cohorts were analyzed (Amsterdam Dementia Cohort: 313 patients, 121 controls; Genetic Investigation in Frontotemporal Dementia study: 102 patients, 102 controls). GrimAge2 was used to estimate epigenetic age acceleration. Associations with diagnosis were assessed using linear regression models adjusted for sex, estimated cell type proportions, and smoking (self‐reported and DNA methylation‐derived), followed by random‐effects meta‐analysis. Component‐level analyses examined smoking‐related DNA methylation, inflammatory markers, and glucose metabolism. Results: Patients with frontotemporal dementia showed increased GrimAge2‐derived epigenetic age acceleration ( β = 1.17 ± 0.36, 95% CI 0.46–1.88, p = 0.001) compared with controls. Component‐level analyses showed increased smoking‐related DNA methylation, systemic inflammation (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 1, C‐reactive protein), and glucose metabolism (glycated hemoglobin; all p < 0.05). Adjustment for smoking‐related DNA methylation was associated with attenuation of the effect estimate by approximately 48% (epigenetic age acceleration: β = 0.62 ± 0.32, 95% CI −0.01–1.24, p = 0.053). Interpretation: Accelerated epigenetic aging in frontotemporal dementia is associated with GrimAge2‐derived DNA methylation patterns linked to smoking, inflammation, and metabolic pathways. These findings raise the possibility that smoking‐related DNA methylation reflects differences in smoking exposure or disease‐related behavioral changes captured by GrimAge2. ANN NEUROL 2026

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Patients with frontotemporal dementia exhibit accelerated epigenetic aging determined by GrimAge2 (β = 1.17 ± 0.36, 95% CI 0.46–1.88, p = 0.001), which is substantially mediated by smoking-related DNA methylation, inflammation, and metabolic signals.

title: Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
abstract: Importance: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a progressive neurological disorder characterized by cerebral ventricular enlargement that is typically associated with gait impairment and often urinary dysfunction and cognitive decline in older adults. iNPH prevalence is approximately 1% to 4% among individuals 65 years and older and 6% to 8% among those 80 years and older. Observations iNPH is a multifactorial disorder involving interactions among cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, vascular dysfunction, and white matter injury. Unlike secondary NPH, iNPH occurs without a known antecedent event such as subarachnoid hemorrhage. Gait disturbance, including a broad-based, slow, shuffling gait and impaired turning, occurs in 85% to 95% of patients with iNPH and is often the earliest symptom. Urinary dysfunction occurs in approximately 75% to 90% of patients with iNPH and commonly includes urgency, nocturia, urge incontinence, or leakage. Cognitive impairment is reported in 60% to 80% of patients with iNPH, predominantly involving impaired attention, processing speed, working memory, verbal fluency, and cognitive flexibility. iNPH is diagnosed primarily based on characteristic clinical findings and neuroimaging (typically brain magnetic resonance imaging) demonstrating cerebral ventricular and subarachnoid space enlargement. Although necessary for diagnosis, these neuroimaging findings are not reliably associated with response to treatment. Early diagnosis of NPH is important because shorter symptom duration and less advanced disease are associated with more favorable outcomes. Patients being evaluated for iNPH should undergo large-volume lumbar puncture with removal of 30 to 50 mL of CSF to confirm the diagnosis and predict shunt responsiveness, measured as improvement in objective gait measures starting within hours after drainage. Extended lumbar drainage with removal of 200 to 300 mL of CSF over several days in an inpatient setting provides higher prognostic accuracy, and may be performed in patients with high clinical suspicion and a negative or equivocal clinical response to lumbar puncture. Treatment for iNPH is CSF diversion with shunt placement, most commonly performed with ventriculoperitoneal shunts, although ventriculoatrial and lumboperitoneal shunts may have similar efficacy. After shunting, approximately 75% to 80% of patients have gait velocity improvement; cognitive and urinary improvements occur in approximately 50% to 70%. Complications of shunts include overdrainage and underdrainage (10%-30%), presenting as postural headaches and subdural collections, and recurrence or worsening of iNPH symptoms, shunt malfunction (10%-20%), and shunt infections (<1%-2%). Conclusions and Relevance iNPH affects approximately 1% to 4% of adults 65 years and older and is associated with gait impairment, cognitive decline, and urinary dysfunction. Symptoms improve in approximately 70% to 90% of patients with iNPH who undergo shunt surgery.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) affects 1% to 4% of adults over 65 years and presents with gait disturbance (85%-95%), urinary dysfunction (75%-90%), and cognitive impairment (60%-80%). Shunt surgery yields gait velocity improvement in 75% to 80% of patients, and cognitive or urinary improvements in 50% to 70%.

title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy
abstract: Importance: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk. Objective: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026. Exposures: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use. Main Outcome and Measures: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios. Results: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups. Conclusions and Relevance: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In this pooled cohort analysis, late-onset epilepsy (LOE) was significantly associated with vascular risk factors, notably a history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), and current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), suggesting that LOE reflects underlying cerebrovascular disease burden.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015–2022; prospective phase, 2023–2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of −1.73 percentage points (95% CI, −3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37–1.21]; P =0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion ( P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In a target trial emulation of cerebral venous thrombosis, initial DOAC therapy met noninferiority criteria compared to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent VTE (weighted risk 3.74% vs 5.47%; risk difference −1.73 percentage points [95% CI, −3.76 to 0.30]; subdistribution HR 0.67 [95% CI, 0.37–1.21]; P for noninferiority=0.004).

title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke
authors: De Los Rios La Rosa Felipe
abstract: BACKGROUND: The burden of stroke is unequally distributed in the United States, with Black individuals experiencing more incident stroke. It remains unclear whether Black individuals also experience worse stroke recovery. We sought to study disparities in longitudinal functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke in a population-based study. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky region over an 18-month period (July 2019 to December 2020). All acute ischemic stroke events were captured. The modified Rankin Scale scores were determined at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months for patients who survived the index event. We studied the association between Black race and longitudinal modified Rankin Scale (across all time points) with mixed-effects ordinal regression, initially adjusting for age, sex, and time since stroke. Hierarchical regression was used to sequentially adjust for stroke severity and management, premorbid health, and social determinants. RESULTS: Among 2796 patients with acute ischemic stroke (mean age, 69.0; 31% Black; 52% female), 2537 survived and were included (mean age, 68.4; 32% Black; 52% female). Black race was associated with a worse longitudinal modified Rankin Scale score (cOR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89–3.60]). Excluding patients with recurrent events did not change this association (cOR, 2.69 [95% CI, 1.92–3.78]). Adding variables reflecting initial stroke severity and management partly attenuated the association (cOR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.43–2.60]). Adding variables reflecting premorbid health further attenuated the association (cOR decreased to 1.43 [95% CI, 1.09–1.87]). The remaining association between Black race and the modified Rankin Scale score was fully attenuated by social determinants, with cOR, 1.09 (95% CI, 0.80–1.47). There was no interaction between race and time since stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Starting at discharge and persisting out to 12 months, acute ischemic stroke functional outcomes are worse among Black individuals. These disparities are significantly attenuated by clinical factors and social determinants; future studies should explore whether the social determinants can be intervened upon in the recovery period.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Black stroke survivors experience significantly worse longitudinal functional outcomes (mRS) up to 12 months post-stroke compared to white individuals (fully adjusted cOR, 1.09 [95% CI, 0.80–1.47] from an initial cOR of 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89–3.60]). These disparities are driven primarily by baseline clinical factors and fully mediated by social determinants of health.

title: Multiomics Profiling Supports Cathepsin B as a Protective Factor in White Matter Hyperintensities and Cognition
abstract: BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a common brain magnetic resonance imaging marker of cerebral small vessel disease and a major risk factor for stroke and dementia, yet the molecular mechanisms governing lesion formation remain incompletely understood. We sought to identify circulating proteins that lie upstream of WMH and influence related clinical manifestations. METHODS: We conducted a 4-stage proteogenomic study. Stage 1 tested a WMH polygenic risk score against 2923 plasma proteins in 52 560 UK Biobank participants (mean age, 56.8 years, 53.9% female, 94.0% White), and candidate proteins against WMH volume in the neuroimaging subset (n=5443; mean age 54.2 years, 53.5% female). Stage 2 applied bidirectional Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and local genetic correlation using cis protein quantitative trait locus and cis expression quantitative trait locus instruments from plasma, vascular, and brain tissue. Stage 3 analyzed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 8 postmortem periventricular white matter samples (4 WMH lesions, 4 controls; mean age, 81 years; 50% female). Stage 4 tested circulating and genetically predicted protein levels against general cognitive ability. RESULTS: Stages 1 and 2 converged on CTSB (cathepsin B) and ECHDC3 (enoyl-coenzyme A hydratase domain–containing 3). Higher plasma CTSB was associated with lower WMH volume (β=−0.09 [95% CI, −0.13 to −0.05]; n=5260), and Mendelian randomization estimates were directionally consistent across all 5 instrument sets (plasma protein quantitative trait locus β=−0.052 [95% CI, −0.064 to −0.040]), with concordant effects on white matter microstructure, perivascular spaces, and lacunar stroke. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing showed CTSB downregulation within lesions, predominantly in astrocytes (log 2 fold change=−1.70) and oligodendrocytes (log 2 fold change=−0.48; both false discovery rate P <1×10 −20 ). Higher plasma CTSB (β=0.061 [95% CI, 0.010–0.112]; n=5193) and a cis protein quantitative trait locus polygenic score (β=0.031 [95% CI, 0.009–0.054]; n=8884) predicted better cognitive performance. ECHDC3 showed no consistent association beyond stage 1. CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal proteogenomic evidence nominates CTSB as a lesion-suppressed protein associated with lower WMH burden and better cognition, and a candidate therapeutic target for cerebral small vessel disease.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Multimodal proteogenomic evidence identifies cathepsin B (CTSB) as a protective factor against cerebral small vessel disease, where higher plasma levels are associated with reduced white matter hyperintensity volume (plasma pQTL β=−0.052, 95% CI, −0.064 to −0.040) and better general cognitive performance (β=0.061, 95% CI, 0.010–0.112).

title: Association of Enlarged Perivascular Spaces and Total Small Vessel Disease Burden With Kidney Function
abstract: Background and Objectives: Enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVS) in the basal ganglia (BG-EPVS) and centrum semiovale (CSO-EPVS) are established neuroimaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) and cerebral amyloid angiopathy. We investigated the associations between EPVS severity, total cSVD burden, and kidney function—including both impaired estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and glomerular hyperfiltration—in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Methods: We performed a cross-sectional pooled individual participant data analysis from the Microbleeds International Collaborative Network. Kidney function was categorized into normal filtration (eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² without hyperfiltration), impaired kidney function (eGFR 30–60 or <30 mL/min/1.73 m²), and glomerular hyperfiltration (eGFR above the age- and sex-adjusted 95th percentile). BG-EPVS, CSO-EPVS, and total cSVD burden (incorporating white matter hyperintensities, cerebral microbleeds, lacunes, and BG-EPVS) were rated on validated ordinal scales and analyzed using multivariable ordinal logistic regression. Results: Among 7,254 patients with ischemic stroke or TIA (mean age 71 years, 43% female), 357 had glomerular hyperfiltration, 1,692 had eGFR 30–60, and 256 had eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m². Compared with normal kidney function, glomerular hyperfiltration was independently associated with greater severity of BG-EPVS (adjusted OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.11–1.70, p < 0.001) and CSO-EPVS (adjusted OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.08–1.64, p = 0.011), as well as higher total cSVD burden. Conclusions: Glomerular hyperfiltration is independently associated with enlarged perivascular spaces in both the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale after ischemic stroke or TIA, supporting shared microvascular hemodynamics between cerebral and renal arterioles.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In a pooled analysis of 7,254 ischemic stroke/TIA patients, renal glomerular hyperfiltration was independently associated with more severe basal ganglia enlarged perivascular spaces (aOR 1.38, 95% CI 1.11–1.70, p < 0.001) and centrum semiovale EPVS (aOR 1.34, 95% CI 1.08–1.64, p = 0.011).

title: Salivary Dim‐Light Melatonin Onset is Associated with Functional Decline, Respiratory Symptom Emergence, and Survival in Early Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
abstract: Objective: Sleep–wake and circadian disturbances are increasingly recognized in people living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (plwALS), but endogenous circadian phase timing and its prognostic significance in early disease remain unclear. We assessed whether salivary dim‐light melatonin onset (DLMO), an objective marker of central circadian phase, is altered in early plwALS and whether it provides prognostic information. Methods: In this prospective longitudinal observational study, plwALS within 18 months of symptom onset underwent home‐based salivary melatonin sampling under dim‐light conditions at 6 predefined time points around habitual sleep onset. Melatonin profiles were modeled using cubic smoothing splines, and DLMO was defined when the fitted curve first reached 3 pg/ml. Clinical, respiratory, and sleep assessments were collected at baseline (T0) and after 6 months (T6); a subgroup repeated saliva sampling at T6. Age‐ and sex‐matched controls underwent melatonin profiling. Associations with disease progression, incident respiratory symptoms, and survival/tracheostomy were examined using regressions and survival analyses. Results: A total of 50 plwALS were enrolled. Compared with controls, plwALS showed an earlier DLMO (20:24 ± 1:18 vs 20:58 ± 0:50; p = 0.028) despite similar habitual sleep onset and chronotype. Within ALS cohort, a later baseline DLMO correlated with worse functional/motor status, faster progression of disease, incident dyspnea/orthopnea by T6 (adjusted OR 3.11; p = 0.019), and poorer survival/tracheostomy‐free outcome. In the resampled subgroup ( n = 28), DLMO and melatonin‐derived metrics did not change over ~6 months. Interpretation: Circadian phase alterations are detectable in early ALS. Baseline DLMO showed exploratory associations with functional, respiratory, and survival outcomes. Larger independent cohorts are required before DLMO can be considered a validated prognostic biomarker. ANN NEUROL 2026

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In early amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a later baseline salivary dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) is associated with worse functional status, faster disease progression, poorer survival/tracheostomy-free outcomes, and increased odds of incident dyspnea or orthopnea at 6 months (adjusted OR 3.11, p = 0.019).

title: Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
abstract: Health literacy is a critical component of high-quality stroke care. Across the continuum from prevention through recovery, health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke-related morbidity. Despite its importance, it is often overlooked, leaving patients and caregivers overwhelmed by communication demands that exceed their capacity. These mismatches are especially pronounced among individuals with stroke-related cognitive or language impairments, limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, or limited digital literacy. This scientific statement synthesizes current evidence on the role of health literacy and communication within stroke systems of care and identifies nurse-led opportunities to advance equity and patient-centered outcomes while recognizing this as a shared interprofessional responsibility. Nurse-led interventions, including teach-back–based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, have demonstrated improvements in stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness. However, the literature is marked by methodological heterogeneity. Many studies are underpowered and infrequently use validated health literacy or communication measures. Future directions include standardized assessment of health literacy; literacy-sensitive, nurse-led, and interprofessional care models; workforce training in plain-language and culturally responsive communication; and organizational health literacy principles. Emerging technologies, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, offer promise for improving communication and personalization but require rigorous evaluation to minimize bias and ensure equity and usability.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Health literacy mismatches strongly impact stroke outcomes, yet the supporting literature suffers from methodological heterogeneity and a lack of validated measures. Practicing neurologists should implement nurse-led, literacy-sensitive communication strategies—such as teach-back education and tailored digital support—while ensuring emerging AI and telehealth tools are rigorously evaluated to maintain equity.

title: Clinical Outcome Differences in Asia Versus Non-Asia Intracerebral Hemorrhage: IPD Analysis From BP-Lowering Clinical Trials
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence of regional differences in clinical outcomes after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is still scarce. We quantified differential outcomes and response to early intensive blood pressure lowering treatment by region in the Blood pressure in Acute Stroke Collaboration ICH data set. METHODS: This was an observational analysis of pooled individual participant data from 16 completed randomized controlled trials of blood pressure-lowering treatment in acute ICH, based on the Blood pressure in Acute Stroke Collaboration data set. Generalized linear mixed models with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to determine the association between regions (Asia [primarily East and South Asia] versus non-Asia) and clinical outcomes including neurological deterioration within 7 days, hematoma expansion at 24 hours (absolute ≥6 mL or relative ≥33%), and death or dependency (modified Rankin Scale scores, 3–6), major disability(modified Rankin Scale score, 3–5), death alone at 90 days. RESULTS: Among 6221 patients (age, 63.3±13.0 years; female 36.4%), 3494 (56.2%) were from Asia. ICH participants from Asia had a significantly reduced risk of death or dependency (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.44 [95% CI, 0.39–0.51]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.58–0.77]); and major disability (unadjusted OR, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.42–0.56]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.57–0.78]) at 90 days, neurological deterioration (unadjusted OR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.52–0.77]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.56–0.89]) within 7 days, in comparison to those from non-Asia regions. However, there were no differences for hematoma expansion ( P =0.97) at 24 hours or death ( P =0.23) at 90 days using IPTW. Additionally, there were no significant interactions between blood pressure–lowering treatment and region (Asia versus non-Asia) for either outcome using IPTW. CONCLUSIONS: Participants from East and South Asia had a favorable functional recovery and a lower risk of neurological deterioration compared with those from non-Asian regions after adjustment for confounders, with no differences in hematoma expansion at 24 hours after ICH. These findings suggest that future ICH studies on clinical outcomes should consider regional differences.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Following acute intracerebral hemorrhage, Asian patients demonstrated a significantly lower risk of death or dependency (IPTW-weighted OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.58–0.77]), major disability (OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.57–0.78]), and neurological deterioration (OR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.56–0.89]) at 90 days compared with non-Asian patients, despite similar rates of hematoma expansion.

title: Mild Amyloid Burden in the Brains of Cognitively Unimpaired Individuals is Associated with Long‐Term Cognitive Impairment
abstract: Objective: We aimed to identify the minimal amount of amyloid burden measured by positron emission tomography (PET) in amyloid‐negative cognitively unimpaired individuals that predicts the development of cognitive impairment. Methods: A total of 1,896 cognitively unimpaired participants underwent longitudinal clinical/cognitive assessments for up to 20.3 years after amyloid PET imaging. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess how the risk of cognitive impairment was associated with subthresholds of amyloid PET Centiloid. Linear mixed effects models were used to associate the longitudinal cognitive decline and amyloid accumulation with baseline amyloid burden. Results: Amyloid‐positive participants (Centiloid >20; n = 421) were 154% (hazard ratio 2.54, p < 0.0001) more likely to develop cognitive impairment than amyloid‐negative participants. Approximately 48.7% of the amyloid‐negative participants had mild amyloid burden (defined by Centiloid from 0.93 to 20) and were 43% more likely to develop cognitive impairment (hazard ratio 1.43, p = 0.008) than the lowest amyloid group (Centiloid <0.93) approximately 10 years post baseline. Longitudinal changes in amyloid PET Centiloid and cognition followed a similar pattern: amyloid‐positive participants were the fastest, followed by the mild amyloid burden group and finally the lowest amyloid group, and the cognitive trajectories for the latter 2 started to separate only approximately 10 years post baseline ( p = 0.003). Interpretation: Almost half of amyloid‐negative cognitively unimpaired individuals were at an elevated long‐term risk of cognitive impairment, when compared with those with the lowest amyloid levels. These findings suggest that the current threshold for amyloid positivity may be overly restrictive, potentially excluding a large portion of high‐risk participants from prevention trials. ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Among cognitively unimpaired individuals currently classified as amyloid-negative, those with mild amyloid burden (Centiloid 0.93–20) face a 43% increased long-term risk of developing cognitive impairment compared to the lowest amyloid group (HR 1.43, p = 0.008), suggesting current positivity thresholds may be overly restrictive for clinical trials.

title: Hemispheric Asymmetry of Neuroimaging Biomarkers in Early Onset Alzheimer's Disease: Clinical and Cognitive Outcomes
abstract: Objective: Individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease (AD) often exhibit amyloid, tau, and atrophy predominantly in the left or right hemisphere, but group‐level analyses typically ignore inter‐individual variability and changing asymmetry patterns when averaging data across participants in phenotypically diverse cohorts. Methods: We examined left/right hemispheric asymmetry in amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), tau PET, and cortical atrophy in sporadic early‐onset AD from 585 deeply phenotyped individuals across 2 cohorts to investigate its clinical correlates. For each imaging biomarker, we computed a global asymmetry index reflecting left/right hemisphere signal difference, and an analogous asymmetry value for PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) voxels. We examined clinical and cognitive correlates of this asymmetry across phenotypes cross‐sectionally and longitudinally in a subset of 218 participants. Results: Both left and right asymmetry were common for all clinical phenotypes and was correlated between imaging biomarkers. Asymmetry patterns varied spatially within phenotypes, and asymmetry in tau PET and MRI volumes was related to hemisphere‐dependent cognitive deficits and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Longitudinal analyses revealed stable amyloid PET asymmetry, decreasing tau PET asymmetry, and increasing MRI volume asymmetry. Interpretation: Hemispheric asymmetry is common in early onset AD and correlates with clinical outcomes. Our longitudinal findings suggest a time‐lagged asymmetry peak in amyloid, then tau, then atrophy. Taken together, our results position asymmetry as an important feature of AD heterogeneity, as it provides insight into disease mechanisms and trajectories. ANN NEUROL 2026

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In early-onset Alzheimer's disease, hemispheric asymmetry is common and correlates with region-specific cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Longitudinal trajectories demonstrate a time-lagged sequence of peak asymmetry, progressing from amyloid PET to tau PET and finally to cortical atrophy.

title: Thrombolysis in the Delayed Treatment Window for Acute Ischemic Stroke: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravenous thrombolysis is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but has traditionally been limited to 4.5 hours after symptom onset. This time-based restriction may exclude patients with salvageable brain tissue, especially those with wake-up or unknown-onset strokes. Multimodal imaging allows for the identification of viable penumbra beyond traditional treatment windows. This study compiles randomized evidence evaluating intravenous thrombolysis in imaging-selected patients treated after 4.5 hours. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central were searched through February 2026 for randomized trials comparing intravenous thrombolysis (alteplase or tenecteplase) with best medical therapy in patients presenting beyond 4.5 hours or with wake-up/unknown-onset stroke selected by imaging. The primary outcome was excellent functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale score 0–1). Secondary outcomes included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0–2), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and 90-day mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen trials involving 4192 participants were analyzed. Intravenous thrombolysis improved excellent functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–1; risk ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.16–1.29]) and functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0–2; risk ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.06–1.18]). Both alteplase and tenecteplase contributed to these benefits. Thrombolysis increased the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (risk ratio, 2.58 [95% CI, 1.58–4.22]) but did not significantly affect 90-day mortality (risk ratio, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.97–1.35]). CONCLUSIONS: In patients selected using advanced imaging, intravenous thrombolysis performed after 4.5 hours improves functional outcomes without increasing mortality, supporting a tissue-based rather than strictly time-based approach to treating acute ischemic stroke.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In acute ischemic stroke patients selected via advanced imaging beyond 4.5 hours (including unknown-onset/wake-up), intravenous thrombolysis significantly improves excellent functional outcomes (mRS 0–1; RR 1.22 [95% CI, 1.16–1.29]) and functional independence (mRS 0–2; RR 1.12 [95% CI, 1.06–1.18]), despite an increased risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (RR 2.58 [95% CI, 1.58–4.22]) without affecting mortality (RR 1.15 [95% CI, 0.97–1.35]).

title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Percentage by Race and Ethnicity in Preclinical Alzheimer Disease
abstract: Importance: In trials targeting preclinical Alzheimer disease (AD), defined as amyloid pathology without cognitive symptoms, racial and ethnic differences in plasma phosphorylated tau 217 percentage (%p-tau217) may influence screening eligibility. Objective: To characterize racial and ethnic differences in %p-tau217 and determine whether associations between %p-tau217, cognition, and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) differ across groups. Design, Setting, and Participants: This was a cross-sectional analysis of AHEAD 3-45 screening participants conducted from July 2020 to October 2024 at 106 sites across 4 world regions. Adults aged 55 to 80 years with %p-tau217 measured before medical and cognitive exclusions (N = 15 612) were included. Exposures: Self-reported race (Asian, Black, and White) and ethnicity (Hispanic and non-Hispanic) and apolipoprotein E ε4 ( APOE ε4) carrier status. Main Outcomes and Measures %p-tau217 levels and associations of %p-tau217 with Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) score and amyloid PET were evaluated across racial and ethnic groups using multivariable linear regression. Results: Among 15 612 participants, the mean (SD) age was 68.4 (6.2) years; 9941 (63.7%) were female and 5755 (36.9%) were APOE ε4 carriers. %p-tau217 levels were lower among Asian, Black, and Hispanic participants than among White and non-Hispanic participants. APOE ε4 status was associated with higher %p-tau217 across all groups. The association between APOE ε4 status and %p-tau217 differed by race ( APOE ε4 × race: F 2,14 973 = 10.06; P < .001) and ethnicity ( APOE ε4 × ethnicity: β, 0.042; 95% CI, 0.017 to 0.067; P = .005) (Asian: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P = .01; Black: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.08; P = .002; Hispanic: β, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.07; P = .005). The %p-tau217–PACC5 association showed no pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, −0.53; 95% CI, −0.85 to −0.21; P = .008) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.26 to 1.30; P = .02). The %p-tau217–PET association showed no significant pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, −6.30; 95% CI, −9.10 to −3.51; P < .001) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 7.12; 95% CI, 2.52 to 11.73; P = .01). Conclusions and Relevance: In this cross-sectional study, plasma %p-tau217 varied across racial and ethnic groups. Consistent %p-tau217–PACC5 score and %p-tau217–PET associations across racial groups support plasma-based screening before PET confirmation, while ethnicity-related findings warrant further investigation.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Plasma %p-tau217 levels are lower in Asian, Black, and Hispanic preclinical Alzheimer disease screening participants compared to White and non-Hispanic individuals. While %p-tau217 associations with cognition and amyloid PET remain consistent across racial groups, significant variations by ethnicity and *APOE* ε4 status require cautious interpretation to prevent screening disparities.

title: Early Pregnancy Use of Anti-CGRP Monoclonal Antibodies and Propranolol and Spontaneous Abortion Risk
abstract: Importance: Migraine affects individuals of reproductive age, but treatment options during pregnancy are limited due to safety concerns. Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are effective for migraine prevention; however, CGRP is important in placental development. Objective: To determine whether early pregnancy exposure to anti-CGRP mAbs or propranolol is associated with spontaneous abortion compared with no exposure. Design, Setting, and Participants: This retrospective cohort study used data from the AM-PREGNANT cohort, derived from the Merative MarketScan Commercial Database, from 2018 to 2021. Participants were followed up through 20 weeks’ gestation or until spontaneous abortion or censoring. Among 7 991 200 pregnancies identified in the AM-PREGNANT cohort, 7119 individuals contributing 7579 singleton pregnancies met the predefined eligibility criteria, including age 15 to 45 years, continuous insurance enrollment, last menstrual period (LMP) on or after November 1, 2018, pregnancy end or 20-week censoring by December 31, 2021, and pregestational migraine, defined as a migraine diagnosis or triptan or ergot prescription within 6 months before LMP. Data were analyzed in early 2026. Exposures: Anti-CGRP mAbs (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, eptinezumab) or propranolol, defined as 1 or more filled prescription or injection procedure claim during follow-up and modeled as time-varying. Main Outcome and Measures: Spontaneous abortion occurring at 20 weeks’ or less gestation. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for comorbidities and concomitant medications estimated the risk of spontaneous abortion. Results: Among 7579 pregnancies in 7119 individuals (mean [SD] age, 31.6 [5.5] years), 1862 spontaneous abortions occurred. There were 100 spontaneous abortions (28.6%) during anti-CGRP mAb-exposed person-time, compared with 37 events among propranolol-exposed person-time without anti-CGRP mAbs (12.8%). Compared with unexposed individuals, anti-CGRP mAbs exposure was associated with an increased risk of spontaneous abortion (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.42; 95% CI, 1.12-1.80), which remained similar in bias-adjusted analyses (HR, 1.33; 95% simulation interval [SI], 1.23-1.45). Propranolol exposure was not associated with increased risk (aHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.71-1.47; bias-adjusted HR, 1.00; 95% SI, 0.96-1.03). Conclusion and Relevance: In this study, early pregnancy exposure to anti-CGRP mAb was associated with a higher risk of spontaneous abortion, while no association was observed with propranolol. These findings support further evaluation of anti-CGRP mAb safety and emphasize counseling for individuals of childbearing potential.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Early pregnancy exposure to anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies is associated with a significantly increased risk of spontaneous abortion (adjusted HR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.12-1.80), whereas propranolol shows no such association (aHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.71-1.47). Clinicians should prioritize proactive counseling for individuals of childbearing potential regarding these safety profiles.

title: Global Incidence of All-Cause Dementia
abstract: Importance: Global dementia incidence estimates are limited by underrepresentation of low- and middle-income countries and heterogeneous analytic methods. Due to these limitations, true understanding of the global dementia landscape remains incomplete. Objective: To identify dementia incidence rates by age and sex in various regions worldwide (high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries) where data on clinically based dementia diagnoses were available. Data Sources Retrospective community-based cohorts from the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (COSMIC); baseline recruitment commenced between January 1990 and December 2011 and follow-up data were collected through the end of 2021. Data were analyzed from June 2024 to June 2025. Study Selection Eligible studies included longitudinal COSMIC cohort studies with a clinically based diagnosis of dementia. Individual participant–level data from 22 population-based longitudinal cohorts (N = 38 418) spanning 18 countries or territories across 6 continents were included. Data Extraction and Synthesis Data extraction and assessment of study quality and validity were conducted according to Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) guidelines. Individual participant–level data were meta-analyzed in a 2-step process using random intercepts for country and study at the global and regional levels and by country income level. Main Outcomes and Measures: For each study with a clinically based diagnosis, incidence rates for all-cause dementia were calculated and a 2-step meta-analysis was conducted. Using a person-years at risk framework with inverse-probability censoring weights and Poisson models, age- and sex-specific incidence were estimated and then standardized to the 2023 global age-sex population structure. Results: Across 287 632 person-years at risk, 3001 participants developed dementia. Age- and sex-standardized incidence was 9.7 (95% CI, 7.89-11.97) per 1000 person-years at risk. Age-standardized incidence was higher in women than men (10.6; 95% CI, 8.61-13.11 vs 8.6; 95% CI, 6.94-10.72). Standardized incidence was higher in low- and middle-income countries (13.6; 95% CI, 9.67-19.24) than in high-income countries (8.3; 95% CI, 6.57-10.54). Applying age- and sex-specific rates to the projected 2050 population yielded a projected 24.7 million new cases, assuming constant incidence over time. Conclusions and Relevance: The harmonized estimates presented in this study provide a comparable benchmark for global dementia incidence and inform planning for prevention, diagnosis, and memory-care services, particularly in underrepresented low- and middle-income country settings.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Global all-cause dementia incidence is 9.7 per 1000 person-years, with higher rates in women (10.6; 95% CI, 8.61-13.11) versus men (8.6; 95% CI, 6.94-10.72) and in low- and middle-income countries (13.6; 95% CI, 9.67-19.24) compared to high-income countries (8.3; 95% CI, 6.57-10.54), projecting 24.7 million new cases globally by 2050.

title: Cerebral No‐Reflow after Thrombectomy: International Delphi Consensus on Definition and Imaging Assessment
abstract: Background: The operational definition and imaging assessment of the no‐reflow phenomenon, a potential contributor to poor clinical outcome despite successful thrombectomy, remains debated. We aimed to develop expert‐based international consensus on the definition, assessment, and reporting standard of cerebral no‐reflow post‐thrombectomy. Methods: Three‐rounds of a modified Delphi web‐based survey was conducted among corresponding authors of peer‐reviewed clinical studies on cerebral no‐reflow between 2020 and 2025. Responses at each round were used to develop structured questionnaires for subsequent rounds. Consensus was predefined as ≥65% agreement. Results: Among 27 panelists, the response rate was 70%, 74%, and 74% over all rounds. There was broad agreement to conceptualize no‐reflow as macrovascular recanalization with impaired microvascular reperfusion. Consensus was reached that macrovascular recanalization is ideally assessed as (1) digital subtraction angiography with expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) grades 2c without clear distal vessel occlusions and/or eTICI 3 only, and (2) absence of a wedge‐shaped time‐to‐maximum (Tmax) or time‐to‐peak (TTP) delay on post‐recanalization perfusion computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Regarding impaired microvascular reperfusion assessment, cerebral blood flow, and/or volume were preferred over time‐based perfusion parameters (Tmax/TTP). The panel expressed a preference that no‐reflow should ideally be assessed ≤6 hours post‐recanalization. Pending formal validation, histopathological–radiological correlation in animal models would sufficiently validate the use of imaging‐based definitions in humans. Interpretation: Based on currently available literature and expert opinions, this Delphi study provides a framework for systematically reporting cerebral no‐reflow after endovascular treatment (EVT). The variability in opinions regarding quantitative thresholds highlights priorities for future methodological standardization and validation studies. ANN NEUROL 2026

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: This international Delphi consensus defines post-thrombectomy cerebral no-reflow as macrovascular recanalization (eTICI 2c without distal occlusion/3, or no wedge-shaped Tmax/TTP perfusion delay) with impaired microvascular reperfusion (assessed preferentially via cerebral blood flow/volume within ≤6 hours), establishing a standardized reporting framework to address persistent clinical outcome disparities.

title: Astrocyte SMN Restoration and Forskolin Treatment Improve SMA Synaptic Pathology
abstract: Objective: Early phenotypic presentation of central afferent synapse dysfunction within patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) represents a key target for therapeutic development; however, the underlying disease mechanisms remain unresolved. By further investigating motor neuron synapse and peri‐synaptic astrocyte process (PAP) defects in human SMA disease pathology, we aimed to develop a novel therapeutic approach to improve motor neuron function. Methods: We utilized healthy subjects and patients with SMA induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)‐derived cultures to assess phenotypes occurring intrinsically within astrocyte processes (monocultures) and at the PAP‐synaptic interface (co‐cultures), respectively, using cell surface capture mass spectrometry proteomics, confocal and super resolution microscopy, synaptogliosome (SG) isolation, and electrophysiology. Results: SMA astrocytes demonstrated intrinsic filopodia actin defects featuring low abundance of actin‐associated cell surface N‐glycoproteins, decreased filopodia density and CDC42‐GTP levels after actin remodeling stimulation, and significantly reduced phosphorylated ezrin, radixin, and moesin (pERM) proteins. Within the SMA motor neuron and astrocyte co‐cultures, we observed concurrent decreases in synapse number, actin‐associated synapsin I expression, and PAP‐associated expression of pERM proteins. Our dual treatment paradigm using SMN1 gene therapy combined with forskolin treatment to stimulate actin dynamics via increasing cyclic adenosine monophosphate levels resulted in increased branching and filopodia density of SMA astrocytes, and improved synapse formation and function of SMA motor neurons. Interpretation: We define actin‐associated defects impacting astrocyte filopodia dynamics and motor neuron synaptic function in SMA. This shaped our therapeutic approach targeted to SMN‐dependent and actin‐related disease mechanisms, which overall demonstrated improvements in motor neuron function and disease pathology. ANN NEUROL 2026

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In human iPSC-derived models of spinal muscular atrophy, astrocyte-specific actin and synaptic deficits contribute to motor neuron dysfunction. Combining SMN1 gene therapy with forskolin treatment significantly improves astrocyte filopodia dynamics, synapse formation, and motor neuron function.

title: Adjuvant Systemic Hypothermia During Mechanical Thrombectomy (ReCCLAIM II): A Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypothermia reduces ischemic injury in preclinical stroke models, yet translation into the clinical setting remains challenging. We aimed to assess the feasibility of inducing adjuvant systemic hypothermia among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke during mechanical thrombectomy. METHODS: This was a phase II randomized feasibility-controlled trial involving 10 sites in the United States, conducted between May 2019 and May 2024. All eligible patients had confirmed proximal middle cerebral artery or internal carotid artery occlusions, an Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score of 6 to 10, and symptom onset within 24 hours. Patients underwent mechanical thrombectomy and were randomly assigned to either treatment with adjuvant hypothermia using a novel intravascular cooling catheter or standard of care. The primary feasibility end points were the ability to achieve a target temperature of <34 °C within 1 hour of arterial puncture and overall door-to-reperfusion times. The primary safety end point was core-laboratory-adjudicated hemorrhagic conversion within 36 hours, and secondary end points included final infarct volume and serious adverse events. RESULTS: A total of 95 patients were enrolled (29 in the roll-in phase and 66 randomized). The mean age of the randomized cohort was 65±12 years, with a median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 15. Among patients in the treatment arm, 30 of 33 (91%) achieved hypothermia within 1 hour of arterial puncture during thrombectomy, and 23 of 33 (70%) patients were at target temperature (<34 °C) before reperfusion. The median time to hypothermia was 10 minutes (interquartile range [IQR], 7–22) from arterial puncture. There were no significant differences in door-to-reperfusion times (hypothermia: 95 minutes [IQR, 54–116] versus control: 94 minutes [IQR, 77–121]; P =0.70). Final infarct volumes were numerically lower in the hypothermia treatment arm (hypothermia: 11 cm 3 [IQR, 5–42] versus control: 30 cm 3 [IQR, 6–80]; P =0.13), with no significant differences in the rates of hemorrhagic conversion or pneumonia. There was a higher number of serious adverse events in the hypothermia arm (45.5% versus 24.2%; P =0.12), although the trial was not powered for differences in serious adverse events or clinical efficacy. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first clinical trial to demonstrate the feasibility of early and rapid systemic hypothermia as an adjunct therapy during mechanical thrombectomy without delaying time to reperfusion. The potential impact on infarct volumes and serious adverse events, however, warrants further investigation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT03804060.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: The ReCCLAIM II trial demonstrated that rapid adjuvant systemic hypothermia during mechanical thrombectomy is feasible (91% achieved target temperature <34 °C within 1 hour) without delaying reperfusion (95 vs. 94 minutes, P=0.70). However, a higher rate of serious adverse events (45.5% vs. 24.2%, P=0.12) requires further evaluation in adequately powered trials.

title: Parent Perspectives on I-ACQUIRE Therapy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy is increasingly recommended as an evidence-based, intensive treatment for children with hemiparesis, parent perspectives are lacking. I-ACQUIRE, a multicomponent form of Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy, involves substantial parent participation. Child outcomes from the United States 15-site I-ACQUIRE phase 3 clinical trial (2019–2025), partnered with a Parent Council, are presented elsewhere. Here, we examine complementary lived-experience parent data. METHODS: All parents (167) of infants/toddlers with perinatal arterial ischemic stroke and hemiparesis consented to child random assignment to usual treatment (UT), moderate-dose I-ACQUIRE (3 h/d, 5 d/wk over 4 weeks), or high-dose I-ACQUIRE (6 h/d). Parents completed assessments about life- and therapy-related stress, treatment concerns, observations of child progress, and perceived therapy-related responsibilities. RESULTS: Parents of children in the I-ACQUIRE moderate-dose (56) and high-dose group (58), compared with UT (53), reported lower rates of concerns or problems that therapy did not produce clear benefits (≤4% versus 18%), child-therapist interactions (≤2% versus 24%), and parent-therapist interactions (≤2% versus 6%). I-ACQUIRE versus UT parents had higher proportions of positive feelings that therapy was useful (94%–98% versus 83%); interesting (96%–98% versus 79%), important (94%–98% versus 85%), and fun (78%–84% versus 53%); and provided comforting (72%–83% versus 47%) and relaxing benefits (28%–31% versus 17%). In all groups, similar proportions reported their role was stressful (I-ACQUIRE 26%–28%, UT 32%), difficult (I-ACQUIRE 35%–48%, UT 38%), and tiring (I-ACQUIRE 48%–52%, UT 43%). General life stress scores were mostly in the moderate-range category, similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: Parents of I-ACQUIRE children reported higher positive feelings and notably fewer concerns about lack of benefits compared with UT. Across all groups, some parents (<52%) reported treatment-related stress, difficulty, and fatigue. These findings provide new perspectives from parents’ lived experiences to help families and clinicians in treatment decision-making. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT03910075.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In this trial of infants with hemiparesis following perinatal stroke, parents of children receiving moderate- to high-dose I-ACQUIRE reported significantly higher positive feelings about therapy and fewer concerns regarding lack of benefit compared with usual treatment (94%–98% vs 83% useful; ≤4% vs 18% benefit concerns), despite equivalent treatment-related stress and fatigue across groups.

title: Centrum Semiovale Perivascular Spaces Predict First Hemorrhagic Lesion in Asymptomatic Amyloid‐Positive Individuals
abstract: Objective: Identification of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) before its hemorrhagic manifestations remains limited. We aimed to determine whether severe enlarged perivascular spaces in the centrum semiovale (EPVS‐CSO) identify a prehemorrhagic stage of sporadic CAA by predicting the first appearance of CAA‐related hemorrhagic lesions or incident cognitive decline in amyloid‐positive, cognitively unimpaired, hemorrhage‐free older adults. Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of the Anti‐Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4) trial, a phase 3 randomized study in cognitively unimpaired, amyloid‐positive older adults. Participants with baseline hemorrhagic lesions were excluded. Baseline EPVS‐CSO severity was dichotomized as severe versus nonsevere. Severe basal ganglia EPVS, more closely associated with hypertensive small vessel disease, was evaluated as a topographical negative‐control exposure. The primary outcome was incident strictly lobar cerebral microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis. The secondary outcome was longitudinal cognitive trajectories measured by the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite. Results: Among 932 participants (mean age 71.7 ± 4.8 years; 61.3% female), 101 (10.8%) had severe EPVS‐CSO at baseline. Over a median follow up of 5.1 years (IQR 3.3–5.5 years), 33.7% of those with severe EPVS‐CSO developed incident CAA‐related hemorrhagic lesions compared with 13.6% of those with nonsevere EPVS‐CSO (adjusted HR 2.85, 95% CI 1.91–4.25; p < 0.0001). Severe basal ganglia EPVS was not associated with incident hemorrhagic lesions (adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.35–2.18; p = 0.77). Severe EPVS‐CSO was not associated with early cognitive differences, and participants who developed incident hemorrhagic lesions showed more pronounced cognitive decline. Interpretation: These findings identify severe EPVS‐CSO as a strong predictor of first appearance of CAA‐related hemorrhagic lesions in amyloid‐positive individuals, supporting integration of amyloid biomarkers into magnetic resonance imaging‐based Boston criteria. Identifying markers of the transition of CAA from a nonhemorrhagic to a hemorrhagic stage provides a potential foundation for approaching primary prevention of CAA‐related hemorrhage. ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: In asymptomatic, amyloid-positive older adults, severe centrum semiovale perivascular spaces (EPVS-CSO) strongly predict the first appearance of CAA-related hemorrhagic lesions (adjusted HR 2.85, 95% CI 1.91–4.25; p < 0.0001), whereas severe basal ganglia EPVS shows no association, supporting their integration into prehemorrhagic CAA risk stratification.

title: Neural Repair Therapies After Stroke: II. Principles for Clinical Trials
abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of human disability worldwide. Additional approaches beyond acute stroke therapies are needed to improve patient outcomes. Neural repair therapies focus on promoting neural plasticity in surviving tissue rather than modifying the acute injury; examples include behavioral training, drugs, biological therapies, and neural stimulation. This review discusses principles related to patient selection, control group design, intervention timing, choice of outcome measures, experience-dependent plasticity, use of biomarkers, and statistical considerations, each of which emerges from a review of key stroke recovery trials. Patient selection strategies may benefit from incorporating neuroimaging and neurophysiology biomarkers to ensure viability of treatment targets. Modality-specific outcome measures offer advantages over global disability scales for repair-based trials. The timing of intervention is critical given evolving poststroke biology and the existence of critical periods for plasticity. Repair-based therapies benefit from pairing with concomitant experience of sufficient intensity and appropriate type to shape and reinforce brain circuits. Consideration of these key principles is expected to improve the design of trials that aim to promote neural repair and improve function after stroke. Researchers and clinicians should attend to these factors when designing and interpreting clinical trials to maximize the likelihood that neural repair therapies will improve disability after stroke.

ai_takeaways.conclusion_vi: Neural repair trials require careful patient selection using biomarkers, optimal timing within critical plasticity windows, and pairing therapies with intensive, modality-specific behavioral training. Because no statistical outcomes, effect sizes, or confidence intervals were reported in this methodological review, trial designs must prioritize these principles to effectively reduce long-term poststroke disability.
